definition: To come upon or occur as something extraneous, additional, or unexpected — to follow closely upon something else, often altering or interrupting it.
etymology: From Latin supervenire, built from super (over, upon) and venire (to come). Roman jurists used it when an unforeseen circumstance arrived to complicate a contract already in motion — something coming over the top of what was already there, the way a late-summer storm supervenes on an otherwise settled afternoon.
usage: August has a way of making you believe the heat is permanent, and then a cool front supervenes overnight, and by morning the whole season has shifted its weight.
